lines.text: Scientists, engineers and game designers use computers to run an experiment thousands of times in a second. That’s simulation.
pick random gives an unpredictable number in a range.
Computers use clever formulas, so they’re called pseudo-random — good enough for simulations.
pick random 1 to 2: call 1 heads and 2 tails.
Repeat 100 times and count the heads.
Theory says heads half the time.
One experiment won’t give exactly 50 — but the more flips, the closer you get.
This is the law of large numbers.
Some problems are too hard to work out by hand.
Simulate them many times and look at the results instead.
The same simulation in Python uses random.randint. Each run gives a slightly different answer.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
